extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry/anabelian geometry (specialists in Mochizuki's IUT theory)
extracted.subtask_description: Formal definitions and structural criteria for Frobenioid-prime-strips (holomorphic, mono-analytic, globally realiﬁed variants) together with associated pseudo-monoids, coric/Kummer structures, and algorithmic reconstruction statements appearing in IUT I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holomorphic Frobenioid-prime-strip (F-prime-strip) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: We define a holomorphic Frobenioid-prime-strip, or F-prime-strip, [relative to the given initial Θ-data] to be a collection of data ‡F = {‡Fv}v∈V that satisfies the following conditions: (a) if v ∈ Vnon, then ‡Fv is a category ‡Cv which admits an equivalence of categories ‡Cv ∼→ Cv [where Cv is as in Examples 3.2, (iii); 3.3, (i)]; (b) if v ∈ Varc, then ‡Fv = (‡Cv, ‡Dv, ‡κv) is a collection of data consisting of a category, an Aut-holomorphic orbispace, and a Kummer structure such that there exists an isomorphism of collections of data ‡Fv ∼→ Fv [where Fv is as in Example 3.4, (i)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a compound, structural criterion: for non-archimedean places the object must be equivalent to the prescribed category Cv; for archimedean places it must present as a category plus an Aut-holomorphic orbispace and a Kummer structure isomorphic to the reference data. The definition organizes local (v-indexed) conditions into the global notion of an F-prime-strip; subsequent statements treat morphisms and capsules built from such prime-strips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic Frobenioid-prime-strip (F (cid:4)-prime-strip) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: We define a mono-analytic Frobenioid-prime-strip, or F (cid:4)-prime-strip, [relative to the given initial Θ-data] to be a collection of data ‡F(cid:4) = {‡F (cid:4)v}v∈V that satisfies: (a) if v ∈ Vnon, then ‡F (cid:4)v is a split Frobenioid whose underlying Frobenioid ‡C(cid:4)v admits an isomorphism ∼→ F (cid:4)v (as in Examples 3.2, (v); 3.3, (i)); (b) if v ∈ Varc, then ‡F (cid:4)v is a triple (‡C(cid:4)v, an object of TM(cid:4), and a splitting of the Frobenioid) such that there exists an isomorphism of collections of data ‡F (cid:4)v ∼→ F (cid:4)v (as in Example 3.4, (ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the mono-analytic analogue of the holomorphic prime-strip: split Frobenioid structure at non-archimedean places, with specified splittings and TM(cid:4)-data at archimedean places. The definition again emphasizes isomorphism-to-reference-data as the acceptance criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms of F- and F (cid:4)-prime-strips
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of F- (respectively, F (cid:4)-) prime-strips is defined to be a collection of isomorphisms, indexed by V, between the various constituent objects of the prime-strips. Following §0 conventions, one thus has notions of capsules of F- (respectively, F (cid:4)-) prime-strips and morphisms of capsules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morphisms are required to be isomorphisms at each local index v; capsules and morphisms of capsules are formed accordingly. This provides the categorical notion of equivalence and maps between prime-strip data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Globally realiﬁed mono-analytic Frobenioid-prime-strip definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A globally realiﬁed mono-analytic Frobenioid-prime-strip, or F (cid:4)-prime-strip, is a collection of data ‡F(cid:4) = (‡C(cid:4), Prime(‡C(cid:4)) ∼→ V, ‡F(cid:4), {‡ρv}v∈V) satisfying: (a) ‡C(cid:4) is a category equipped with a Frobenioid structure isomorphic to the category C(cid:4)mod of Example 3.5, (i); (b) Prime(‡C(cid:4)) ∼→ V is a bijection; (d) ‡F(cid:4) = {‡F (cid:4)v}v∈V is an F (cid:4)-prime-strip; (e) each ‡ρv : Φ‡C(cid:3),v ∼→ Φrlf‡C(cid:4)v is an isomorphism of topological monoids (both isomorphic to R≥0); (f) the collection is isomorphic to the collection F(cid:4)mod of Example 3.5, (ii). Morphisms are isomorphisms between such collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a strengthened global realization condition: the underlying category must be globally isomorphic to the reference mod-category, primes must be globally labeled, and local realizations must match prescribed topological monoid identifications. It formalizes when a mono-analytic prime-strip is globally realized in the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-theoretic construction from a D-prime-strip (profinite group and ind-topological monoid)
rubrics_metrics.description: From a D-prime-strip ‡D = {‡Dw}w∈V and v ∈ Vnon one may construct group-theoretically from π1(‡Dv), in a functorial fashion, a profinite group corresponding to 'Cv' (containing π1(‡Dv) as an open subgroup) and an ind-topological monoid Mv(‡Dv) equipped with its natural π1(‡Dv)-action; one then constructs pseudo-monoids of κ-, ∞κ-, and ∞κ×-coric rational functions Mκv(‡Dv), M∞κv(‡Dv), M∞κ×v(‡Dv) equipped with their natural πrat1(‡Dv)-actions, identifying Mv(‡Dv)× with M∞κ×v(‡Dv)× where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page asserts algorithmic/functorial constructibility of these objects from π1(‡Dv) using the algorithms/theorems from AbsTopII/III and related references. The identification/compatibility of invertible elements and invariants is part of the acceptance criterion: these objects must carry the stated π1-actions and admit the stated identifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and uniqueness of ∞κ-coric / ∞κ×-coric structures on ‡Fv
rubrics_metrics.description: ‡Fv always admits an ∞κ-coric (respectively, ∞κ×-coric) structure, which is, moreover, unique up to a uniquely determined isomorphism [i.e., of pseudo-monoids equipped with continuous actions by πrat1(‡Dv)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance requires that the ∞κ-coric (and ∞κ×-coric) structure be constructible and canonical (unique up to unique isomorphism). Subsequent arguments treat these canonically attached structures as given without further notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation of pairs π1(‡Dv) (cid:3) ‡Mv to Frobenioid and notion of ∞κ-coric structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A pair π1(‡Dv) (cid:3) ‡Mv (an ind-topological monoid with π1(‡Dv)-action isomorphic to the canonical pair π1(‡Dv) (cid:3) Mv(‡Dv)) may be regarded as related to the Frobenioid ‡Fv via the unique isomorphism corresponding to the identity automorphism of ‡D; such a pair (resp. its ∞κ- or ∞κ×-versions) is called an ∞κ-coric (resp. ∞κ×-coric) structure on ‡Fv if it is isomorphic (as a pair with πrat1(‡Dv)-action) to the canonical constructions from (v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the acceptance standard for what counts as an ∞κ-coric structure: it must be isomorphic (with πrat-action) to the standard object constructed from π1(‡Dv) and Mv(‡Dv). The isomorphism is required to be the canonical one determined by the identity on ‡D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic reconstruction of Kummer structure cyclotomic isomorphism and pseudo-monoid isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Considering divisors of zeroes and poles and Kummer classes of rational functions (as in AbsTopIII, Proposition 1.6, (iii)) and using the inclusion Q → Ẑ ⊗ Q, there exists a unique isomorphism of cyclotomes μ̂Z(π1(‡Dv)) μΘ ∼→ μ̂Z(‡M∞κv) (resp. for ∞κ×) such that the induced isomorphism between direct limits of cohomology modules yields isomorphisms M∞κv(‡Dv) ∼→ ‡M∞κv (and analogously for M and M×). One may algorithmically reconstruct the Kummer structure cyclotomic isomorphism μΘ and hence the Kummer structure isomorphism Mv(‡Dv)μ ∼→ ‡Mμ from the projective system of coverings of Aut-holomorphic orbispaces and the abstract pseudo-monoid with πrat-action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a precise reconstructibility criterion: from the projective system of coverings and the πrat-action one must be able to recover the cyclotomic μΘ isomorphism and thereby the isomorphisms of the pseudo-monoids of coric functions. The statement emphasizes uniqueness and algorithmicity (functorial constructibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer-ready vs Kummer-blind distinction (ability to perform Kummer theory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain Frobenioids/pseudo-monoids (e.g., †F (cid:6), †F (cid:7), †M(cid:7), †M(cid:7)sol, †M(cid:7)κ-sol, †M(cid:7)∞κ, †M(cid:7)∞κ×) are 'Kummer-ready' (one can perform Kummer theory and hence recover additive/ring/field structures), whereas others (e.g., †F(cid:7)mod, copies/products of †F(cid:7)J, and other objects without the embedding †F(cid:7)mod → †F(cid:7)) are 'Kummer-blind' (one cannot perform Kummer theory; e.g., N-th roots may not exist, so additive structure cannot be recovered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a diagnostic criterion specifying when the Kummer-theoretic reconstruction techniques apply. The page gives concrete examples and consequences (e.g., Kummer-blackout prevents recovery of additive structure unless additional embedding data is provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of pseudo-monoids of coric rational functions as meromorphic functions on Aut-holomorphic orbispaces
rubrics_metrics.description: For archimedean v (v ∈ Varc), the pseudo-monoids of κ-, ∞κ-, and ∞κ×-coric rational functions associated to Cv may be represented, via algorithmic constructions, as pseudo-monoids of 'meromorphic functions' Mκv(‡Dv), M∞κv(‡Dv), M∞κ×v(‡Dv) — i.e., as sets of morphisms from constituents of the projective system ‡Dratv to Mv(‡Dv)gp compatible with tautological co-holomorphicizations and satisfying descent/equivariance conditions. Moreover, Mv(‡Dv)× and M∞κ×v(‡Dv)× are isomorphic, as abstract topological monoids, to S1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance requires that the analytic/Aut-holomorphic-orbispace representation exist and be compatible with the Kummer structure and co-holomorphicization; invertible-element identifications to S1 are part of the expected structure in the archimedean case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstructibility of rational functions from divisors and local Kummer classes (cuspidal inertia action)
rubrics_metrics.description: By considering the action of cuspidal inertia groups on elements of the pseudo-monoid ‡M∞κv (resp. ‡M∞κ×v) — equivalently, local Kummer classes at the points giving rise to these inertia groups — one obtains Q-multiples corresponding to orders of zeroes/poles; since a rational algebraic function is determined by its divisor of zeroes and poles together with its value at a single point, one may algorithmically reconstruct the Kummer-structure-determined isomorphisms of pseudo-monoids Mκv(‡Dv) ∼→ ‡Mκv, M∞κv(‡Dv) ∼→ ‡M∞κv (and analogously for ∞κ×) from the projective system of coverings, the abstract pseudo-monoid with πrat-action, and the collection of splittings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This details the concrete reconstruction method: local Kummer data (cuspidal inertia) yields orders of zeros/poles; combine with value at a point to recover meromorphic functions and hence the full pseudo-monoid isomorphism. Algorithmicity/functoriality and use of splittings are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility and functoriality constraints (πrat-actions, inclusions, and identifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout, constructions/isomorphisms are required to be compatible with continuous actions by π1(—) or πrat1(—), compatible with the integral submonoids O_p discussed earlier, and to respect natural inclusions/equalities (e.g., M∞κ(†D) ⊆ M∞κ×(†D), units inclusions, identifications of invertible parts with M(†D)). Various isomorphisms of cyclotomes and of direct limits of cohomology modules must induce the stated identifications of pseudo-monoids and monoids with their π1-actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a meta-criterion: any claimed construction or isomorphism must respect the stated group actions, inclusions of sub-pseudo-monoids, identifications of invertible elements, and compatibility with previously constructed ring/monoid structures; proofs and algorithms must verify these compatibilities (often by invoking AbsTopII/III theorems).
